 News › News News › Thiruvananthapuram schools to remain closed on November 11: Beemapally Uroos brings local holiday, c… Thiruvananthapuram schools to remain closed on November 11: Beemapally Uroos brings local holiday, check who is exempt
 Adhya Sarna Updated: Nov 10, 2026, 07:31 IST School holiday in Thiruvananthapuram Educational institutions and state government offices within city limits will remain closed on Wednesday in view of the annual festival at the Beemapally Dargah Shareef.
 The Thiruvananthapuram District Collector has declared a local holiday on Wednesday, November 11, on account of the Beemapally Uroos festival. 
 The order, issued by District Collector Anju K. S., applies to all educational institutions and state government offices within the limits of the Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation.
 The holiday marks the opening of one of the most prominent religious festivals in southern Kerala. The Beemapally Uroos, an eleven-day pilgrimage with appeal across faiths, will be held in Thiruvananthapuram from November 11 to 21. 
 The festival is observed annually at the Beemapally Dargah Shareef, and the declaration allows residents and devotees to take part in the opening ceremonies without disruption to their routine.
 What is Uroos? 
 Popularly known as the Chandanakkudam Mahotsavam, the Uroos is widely regarded as a symbol of Kerala's communal harmony. The festival begins with a flag-hoisting ceremony on Jama dul Akbar in the Hijra calendar and continues for eleven days. 
 The dargah draws worshippers of every faith from across the state and beyond, who gather to offer prayers and seek blessings.
 Among its best-known traditions is the offering of earthen pots. Devotees carry pots covered with sandalwood paste and filled with coins as offerings, while art forms such as Daharamuttu, performed with a sword, form part of the celebrations. The shrine is dedicated to Beema Beevi and her son, and the festival is an important part of the cultural life of the coastal Beemapally neighbourhood.
 Implications for the public 
 Under the order, schools, colleges and state government offices within the corporation limits will remain closed on November 11. Similar holidays declared in earlier years carried exemptions. In 2025, for instance, the holiday did not apply to local self-government institutions or to offices engaged in election work, nor to public examinations that had been scheduled in advance. Students, parents and employees are therefore advised to consult the official notification to confirm whether any such exemptions apply this year.
 Residents and visitors should also expect heavier footfall and traffic in and around Beemapally during the festival period. Authorities customarily arrange additional transport services, including special bus operations, to carry pilgrims to the dargah. Special buses are deployed to ferry devotees, and a local holiday is declared in the city. Commuters in the coastal belt are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and to cooperate with traffic and crowd management arrangements.
 What’s next? 
 With the festival continuing until November 21, the district administration, police and civic agencies are expected to coordinate on security, sanitation, drinking water and public safety. Devotees have been encouraged to observe the guidelines issued by the authorities so that the celebrations proceed smoothly.
 The holiday reflects the administration's recognition of the festival's cultural and religious significance, and it extends to the wider city the opportunity to participate in a tradition that has long brought communities together.
